replies.text:
Check (step 2):
- Automated abuse reachable: "Logged-in customers can post comments" on "public product pages" — mass spam posting covered by listed threat 2; flooding covered by listed threat 6. No sign-in/email/SMS form in the design, so no brute-force or mail-flood gap.
- Staff/admin screen showing user-supplied content: yes — "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen." Listed threat 1 names "each moderator's browser" but only as script execution for data theft; abuse of moderator delete powers from that session is a clearly different harm (admin control) — not covered.
- Deleting/moderating with no record of who did it: yes — "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen." No audit record described; listed threat 5 only covers CSRF-forced actions, not accountability for genuine moderator deletions — not covered.
- Personal/financial documents cacheable by browsers/CDNs: design has only public product pages and comments, no personal or account documents — not applicable.
- Attacker-controlled text into logs, CSV exports, emails, headers: design mentions no exports, emails or logging — not applicable.

{
  "schema": "threatline.threatmodel.v1",
  "issueKey": "EVAL-02",
  "sketch": {
    "components": ["comment submission", "product page renderer", "moderator admin screen", "comment delete action"],
    "dataStores": ["comments database"],
    "externalServices": [],
    "trustBoundaries": ["anonymous visitor -> public product page", "logged-in customer -> comment store", "moderator -> admin screen"],
    "dataClasses": ["pii"],
    "exposure": "public",
    "llmFeatures": false
  },
  "threats": [
    {
      "stride": "ElevationOfPrivilege",
      "title": "Comment markup executes in the moderator admin screen and abuses moderation powers",
      "scenario": "A logged-in customer posts a rich-text comment crafted so that its markup runs when a moderator opens the admin screen to triage it. Running inside the moderator's privileged session, the script issues delete requests on the moderator's behalf: it wipes legitimate comments across the whole site and preserves the attacker's own abusive content, or changes anything else the admin screen can reach. The harm is loss of the moderation control plane, not just theft of a visitor's data.",
      "component": "Moderator admin screen",
      "likelihood": 3,
      "impact": 5,
      "rating": { "attacker": "user", "effort": "medium", "reach": "all", "harm": "takeover" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen." },
        { "quote": "Logged-in customers can post comments with rich text (bold, links, images) on public product pages." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V1.5.3", "V5.3.3"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-79", "CWE-272"],
      "plainLanguage": "A nasty comment can hijack a moderator's own screen and use their delete powers to erase everyone else's comments.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Render untrusted comment content inertly in the moderation screen",
        "given": "a stored comment containing active markup such as event handlers, javascript: links or scriptable SVG",
        "when": "a moderator opens the admin screen to review that comment",
        "then": "the comment is shown as inert text or inside a sandboxed, non-privileged context so no submitted content can invoke moderator actions such as comment deletion"
      }
    },
    {
      "stride": "Repudiation",
      "title": "Comment deletions by moderators leave no record of who deleted what",
      "scenario": "The design gives moderators a screen to delete comments but describes no record of the deletion. A moderator (or anyone who has obtained moderator access) removes critical product reviews or a competitor's feedback and can later deny doing it; the affected customer and the business cannot tell whether a comment was deleted, by whom or why, so abuse of moderation goes unseen and incident response after a moderator account compromise has nothing to reconstruct.",
      "component": "Comment delete action / moderator admin screen",
      "likelihood": 4,
      "impact": 3,
      "rating": { "attacker": "insider", "effort": "low", "reach": "many", "harm": "minor" },
      "evidence": [
        { "quote": "Moderators can delete comments from an admin screen." },
        { "quote": "Comments are stored in the comments database and rendered for every visitor." }
      ],
      "asvs": ["V7.1.3", "V7.2.1"],
      "cwe": ["CWE-778"],
      "plainLanguage": "Nothing records which moderator deleted which comment, so unfair or malicious deletions can be denied and never noticed.",
      "requirement": {
        "title": "Audit every comment deletion",
        "given": "a moderator deleting a comment from the admin screen",
        "when": "the delete action succeeds",
        "then": "an append-only audit record is written with the acting moderator identity, comment id, product, timestamp and source address, retained and reviewable independently of the comments database"
      }
    }
  ]
}
